relevance_note: Cohort deep-sequencing study that gives individual-level data (age, sex, variant, phenotype) for three patients with mosaic TNFAIP3 variants: "Three patients with lymphoproliferation had mosaic variants in TNFAIP3 leading to premature termination and haploinsufficiency (Patient IDs 66, 99, and 507)".
method_note: Read the full paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON from values transcribed by reading (no table parsing). Scope: 452 affected + 154 healthy individuals were sequenced; only the three affected patients with TNFAIP3 variants (Patient IDs 66, 99, 507) are in scope. No relatives described. Labels: the paper identifies people by numeric 'Patient ID' (table column 'Patient ID'; text 'Patient ID 507', 'Patient 66', 'Pt. ID 66', 'ID 66 and 99'); used 'Patient ID <n>' throughout, the paper's own convention. All three TNFAIP3 variants are mosaic (VAF 0.016-0.060 in blood); the paper does not say whether they are somatic or gonosomal and they are not tumour-only, so they are recorded with zygosity 'mosaic' and the people kept in scope; the authors explicitly do not diagnose HA20 ('mosaic variants in TNFAIP3 have not been demonstrated to cause mosaic GEI'). Patient 507 also carries a mosaic MAP3K1 p.Val128Met (Table 1/Table 3, UMS), recorded as a second variant row. Age: Table 1 'Age' column gives a bare number with no unit or timepoint; recorded as age at last evaluation in years (the text uses years for other patients' ages from the same column, e.g. '26 y.o. female' for Patient ID 185). Variant type for 507 comes from the Table 1 section header row ('Frameshift') under which its row sits; for 66 and 99 from text. Pathogenicity is the authors' own mosaic scoring category from Table 3 (LMP), not an ACMG class. Disease label is Table 3 'Clin. Pheno' category (LYM/DYS/DEF) with the legend; no person is given an HA20 diagnosis. Functional evidence = ddPCR VAF in purified immune-cell subsets (Figure 4F/G) for 66 and 99; only those two were tested ('PBMC from two patients were tested'), so 507 is not reported. Patient ID 66's variant was also detected in the accompanying exome-reanalysis manuscript by Ghosh et al. (Table 1 dagger; 'Five variants were detected by both methods'); this is a concurrent, not an earlier, publication, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is left null. Clinical details are said to be in Supplemental Table S5, which is not in the file. No stacked cells. No contradictions found (Table 3 lists 99 as DYS and 507 as DEF while the text says all three had lymphoproliferation; both recorded as observed, not contradictory).
